content: Phase 72 plan: docs/phases/jobs-background-tasks-and-ci-watch.md. Adds `tagteam job` — a file-backed (.tagteam/jobs/<id>/), detached, model-free background task with status/log/result — and its first kind, `ci-watch` (--pr / --run / --workflow+--ref / --pypi), answered only via `gh … --json` and PyPI /simple/ (PEP 691). Guards the 2026-09-20 previous-run trap (--workflow --ref ignores runs created before the job started). error ≠ failed (gh missing/unauth/not found ends immediately). Delivery: job.json+log always, one desktop notification (--quiet off), optional --to-lead interjection. CLI start|list|status|log|cancel (reads in READ_ONLY_COMMANDS). Cockpit: DB-free GET /api/jobs + POST /api/jobs/cancel, a Jobs strip shown only when jobs exist; 'lost' derived on read via procs.identity. A job never touches the turn slot (criterion 6). Out: model failure summary (deferred, measure first), starting jobs from the cockpit, other kinds. Open questions for review: files vs DB for records; notify on by default.

The file-backed design, deterministic-only first release, and desktop notifications on by default are reasonable. Please resolve these concrete contract gaps before implementation:

1. Workflow freshness contradicts the main acceptance criterion (docs/phases/jobs-background-tasks-and-ci-watch.md:88,151). A previous successful run created 60 seconds before job start passes the proposed start-minus-two-minutes filter, so the job can report green before the new run appears. Define an unambiguous selection contract: e.g. arm before the trigger and exclude baseline run IDs, or bind to an explicitly supplied expected commit/run identity. Explain how a watch started after the push finds that intended run, how multiple matching runs are resolved, and pin the selected run ID. Include the previous-run-within-the-two-minute-window regression, not only an old run outside it.

2. Lost-job cancellation has no actor that can finish it (lines 59-69,129). Cancel only writes a marker for the sole-writer runner, but a lost runner cannot consume it. Specify how cancellation of a confirmed dead job becomes durably terminal, how it participates in list/retention, and how unverifiable identity differs from confirmed death. Also specify startup ownership: start writes the initial record and records PID/identity after spawn while the child can already write its result. A startup handshake/claim or equivalent must prevent the parent from overwriting a fast child's terminal result and prevent a second `job run ID` from delivering again. Add focused lifecycle cases for fast completion, duplicate runner, and cancel-after-runner-death.

3. PR checks may not exist yet (lines 86,93-94). A watch started immediately after creating/updating a PR can legitimately see no checks before CI registers them. The current blanket nonzero => terminal error makes that common waiting case stop immediately. GitHub CLI's populateStatusChecks explicitly errors when no checks are reported (https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/trunk/pkg/cmd/pr/checks/checks.go). Define a structured way to distinguish an existing PR with checks not yet registered from a missing/inaccessible target, without treating an empty check set as green or scraping localized stderr. Add no-checks -> pending -> terminal fixtures alongside the actual missing/auth failures. JSON export returns before the normal pending/failed exit-code logic in that source, so canned JSON/exit-code pairs should match the real command.

4. Phone delivery is promised without an implementation (Summary and lines 98-101). watcher.notify_macos delegates to tagteam.notify, which only calls osascript/Windows toast/notify-send. It has no Remote Control or phone push transport. Either scope this phase explicitly to best-effort desktop delivery and remove the phone guarantee, or identify and verify the actual phone delivery path with an acceptance check. A stubbed desktop notifier proves only the local call.

Reviewed the plan, roadmap, notification/process/interjection helpers, and GitHub CLI source. No tests run for this plan review. No standing advisory orders or arbiter interjections were present.

Plan r2 (docs/phases/jobs-background-tasks-and-ci-watch.md @ HEAD). All four r1 findings accepted:

1. Workflow selection is now bound to a commit, not a time window. `--ref REF` is resolved once, synchronously at `start`, via `git rev-parse --verify REF^{commit}` (or `--sha SHA` directly); an unresolvable ref fails `start` with no job written. The runner polls `gh run list --workflow NAME --commit SHA` (flag verified on the real gh against v3.14.8's publish run): none → wait, never green; several → pin highest databaseId, log the rest; `pinned_run` recorded and only `gh run view <pinned>` thereafter. A previous run of the same workflow/ref is a different commit, so it can never match however recent. Criterion 2 now includes the 60 s-old previous run, the two-runs-same-sha pin, and the unresolvable ref.

2. Ownership via two O_EXCL tokens. `claim`: start writes job.json (status starting) before spawn and never again; `job run ID` must create `claim` (pid/ident) first — a duplicate exits non-zero writing nothing; if no claim within 5 s, start races for `claim` itself and, if it wins, records `error: runner did not start`. `final`: whoever creates it writes the terminal record and delivers — exactly once. Liveness on read (reader writes nothing): alive / lost (pid dead or identity differs = confirmed) / unknown (pid answers, identity() None — never treated as dead). Cancel: marker always; live runner finalises within one interval; confirmed-lost → cancel takes `final`, writes cancelled/"runner lost", delivers nothing, durable and retention-pruned; unknown → marker only, not finalised. Criterion 4 adds fast completion, duplicate runner, cancel-after-death, unverifiable identity, never-claims.

3. `--pr` uses `gh pr view N --json number,state,headRefOid,statusCheckRollup` instead of `gh pr checks` — existing PR = exit 0 with a (possibly empty) rollup; missing/inaccessible = non-zero = error. Structural, no stderr text. Empty rollup = "no checks registered yet", keep waiting, never green. CheckRun/StatusContext normalised to pending/pass/skip/fail; head sha logged per poll and followed on change; optional `--expect-checks N` for workflows that register one at a time (without it, the limit is named). Fixtures pair JSON with the real command's exit code; criterion 1 adds empty → pending → terminal.

4. Phone guarantee removed. Delivery is best-effort desktop via tagteam.notify (osascript / toast / notify-send); notifier failure logged, never changes the result; phone push via Remote Control is explicitly not tagteam's. Criterion 5 now says it proves only the local call, plus exactly-once under duplicate runner / racing cancel.

The revised commit-bound workflow selection (including its documented same-commit semantics), structured PR rollup handling, and desktop-only delivery resolve those r1 findings. Startup ownership and duplicate-runner exclusion are substantially clearer. One lifecycle issue remains in the new token design:

R1 — Recover an interrupted finalizer; distinguish one writer from exactly-once delivery (docs/phases/jobs-background-tasks-and-ci-watch.md:75-78,99-102). Concrete sequence: the runner creates the O_EXCL `final` file, is killed before replacing job.json, and the job consequently reads lost. Cancel then cannot create `final`, so it cannot perform the promised durable lost -> cancelled transition. The same gap exists if a canceller dies after taking final. The permanent token provides exclusion, not crash recovery.

Please define a recoverable finalization protocol: e.g. an OS-released lock around re-reading/writing the terminal record, or another explicit ownership/recovery mechanism. Concurrent cancellers must recheck the terminal state under that serialization; recovery must never overwrite a committed CI result. Include a test that kills/stubs failure after finalization ownership is acquired but before the terminal write, then verifies Cancel can durably finish the job. Define handling of incomplete claim publication too (O_EXCL creation and writing its pid/identity are separate operations), without interpreting missing identity data as proof an owner is dead.

Also narrow the delivery guarantee to what the protocol can provide. A process can die after committing the terminal record but before notification/interjection, or after sending but before recording delivery. At-most-once best-effort attempts, with a documented possible missed delivery after a crash and no replay on lost-job cleanup, are sufficient for this phase; a crash-proof exactly-once transport is not required. Update the unconditional exactly-once wording and acceptance criteria accordingly, preserving the normal-path and duplicate-runner checks.

Reviewed plan r2 at aba3b2e and the lead submission. No tests run for a plan-only review. No advisory orders or arbiter interjections were present.

Plan r3 (docs/phases/jobs-background-tasks-and-ci-watch.md @ HEAD). R1 accepted — the O_EXCL tokens are gone; ownership is now two OS-released locks using the existing portable primitive (dualwrite._os_lock: fcntl.flock / msvcrt.locking):

- runner.lock — held by the runner for its whole life (the acquire_watcher_lock pattern). Ownership AND liveness: `job run` acquires non-blocking with a 2 s retry (so a reader's momentary probe can't masquerade as a duplicate); failure = duplicate → exit non-zero, nothing written. Holding the lock IS the claim, so there is no "claim created but identity not written" window; pid/ident in job.json are display-only. Descriptors are non-inheritable (PEP 446), so gh children don't keep it.
- job.lock — blocking, short-held around EVERY job.json write (start's deadline, runner, cancel): re-read → change → atomic replace. A terminal record is never replaced (only its committer may add `delivery`), so recovery can't overwrite a committed CI result and concurrent cancellers serialise and re-check. Lock order: runner takes runner.lock once before ever taking job.lock; everyone else only probes runner.lock non-blocking.
- Startup: start writes job.json (starting) + both lock files, spawns; runner (holding runner.lock) moves starting→running under job.lock or exits if terminal; start's 5 s deadline, under job.lock, writes `error: runner did not start` only if still starting. A fast child's result is never touched.
- Liveness on read (reader opens the existing lock read-only, writes nothing): busy → running; acquirable → confirmed dead → lost; unprobeable (missing/unopenable) → unknown, never treated as dead.
- Cancel: marker, then under job.lock: terminal → report; busy → runner finalises within an interval; free (lost — incl. killed after taking job.lock but before the terminal write, or a dead canceller) → cancel commits cancelled/"runner lost" durably, no delivery; unknown → marker only. Cancel never kills.

Delivery narrowed as asked: at most once, best-effort, only by the committer, after releasing job.lock, then records `delivery` under the lock. Documented gaps: death before delivery = missed, never replayed; death after sending but before recording = no `delivery` field. Lost-job cleanup delivers nothing.

Criteria 4/5 add: interrupted finaliser (real child takes both locks, os._exit before terminal write → lost → cancel durable, survives re-read + second cancel); dead canceller after taking job.lock; concurrent cancellers (one commits); recovery never overwrites a committed success; missing lock → unknown, not finalised; probe doesn't block a real start; runner never starts → deadline error, late runner exits; committer killed between commit and delivery → no field, no replay. Normal-path one-notification and duplicate-runner checks kept.

Unrelated in the same push: arbiter deferred Phase 44 (Saloon rethink) indefinitely — roadmap status only, separate commit.

Approved. Reviewed plan r3 at 30dfa1b and the existing dualwrite/watcher locking primitives. The OS-released runner/job locks resolve the interrupted-finalizer issue: writers re-read under serialization, terminal results are preserved, and lost-job cancellation can recover after a holder dies. The proposed real-process crash and concurrent-cancel tests cover the requested recovery cases. Delivery is now explicitly at-most-once and best-effort, with missed/unrecorded delivery after a crash documented and no replay on cleanup.

The earlier target-selection, empty-PR-rollup, startup-ownership, and desktop-delivery findings remain addressed. Implementation should follow the documented lock ordering and use genuinely non-blocking probes (the existing dualwrite._os_lock itself is blocking). This is an implementation detail within the approved design, not another plan revision.

No tests run for this plan review. No advisory orders or interjections were present. The separate Phase 44 deferral is acknowledged and outside this phase's implementation scope.
